THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Spicy Beef & Broccoli Rice Bowls

This replaces takeout beef & broccoli with a 25-minute version that reheats clean, doesn't get soggy, and splits for kids without a single extra step.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME25 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~500 cal | ~45g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Don't overcrowd the pan when searing beef — steaming instead of searing ruins it. Do batches.

Ingredients

RICE

  • 1 cup rice
  • 2 cups Roli Roti Butcher's Bone Broth

SAUCE BASE (SHARED)

  • 2 tbsp soy sauce (or tamari + splash dark soy)
  • 1/2 cup beef broth
  • 1 tsp sesame oil

Option A — Mild Soy Glaze

  • Mini meatballs or beef sausage slices
  • Small splash soy sauce + broth (NO chili)

Option B — Dry Bowl

  • Optional: ketchup or mild dipping sauce on side

VEG

  • 3-4 cups broccoli (fresh or frozen)
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced

ADULT PROTEIN

  • 1.25 lb beef (tri-tip / flank / sirloin), sliced thin
  • 1 tsp cornstarch (velveting)

ADULT FLAVOR BUILD

  • Chili oil or sriracha
  • 1 tsp ginger, grated
  • Sesame seeds
  • Green onion, sliced

Allergens: soy, sesame.

STOP. Rice and broccoli are done. Bowl up the base now — adult bowls get seared beef with spicy sauce, kid bowls get meatballs or sausage with mild soy.

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.COOK RICE. Cook 1:2 ratio with bone broth instead of water. Fluff and set aside. This is your flavor foundation — don't skip.
  2. 2.PREP BEEF. Slice thin against the grain. Toss with 1 tsp soy sauce + 1 tsp cornstarch for velveting. If you mess this up → chewy, game over.
  3. 3.COOK BROCCOLI. High heat stir-fry or air fry. Goal: slightly charred edges, bright green, not mushy. Set aside.

Adult — Spicy Soy-Sesame

  1. 4.SEAR BEEF. Screaming hot pan. Don't overcrowd — do batches. Quick sear 1-2 min per batch.
  2. 5.BUILD SAUCE. Add soy sauce + beef broth + sesame oil + garlic + ginger to pan. Add chili oil or sriracha for heat. Simmer briefly.
  3. 6.COMBINE. Return broccoli, toss quickly. Keep it glossy, not soupy. Serve over bone broth rice. Top with sesame seeds and green onion.

Kid Path — Mild & Familiar · Option A — Mild Soy Glaze

  1. 4.COOK PROTEIN. Heat meatballs or sausage slices separately. Light salt + minimal soy only.
  2. 5.MILD SAUCE. Small splash soy + broth in kid pan. No chili, no sriracha. Keep it light.
  3. 6.COMBINE. Rice + protein + broccoli (on side or mixed lightly). Keep sauce minimal.

Kid Path — Mild & Familiar · Option B — Dry Bowl

  1. 4.BOWL. Rice + meatballs/sausage + broccoli on side. No sauce.
  2. 5.SERVE. Optional dipping sauce on the side. Keep it simple.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Spicy Soy-Sesame: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid Path — Mild & Familiar: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Don't use too much sauce — soggy rice kills the bowl. Keep it glossy, not soupy.
  • Don't overcook broccoli — charred edges and bright green, not army green mush.

If something fails

Beef is chewy / tough: Either sliced too thick, cut with the grain, or skipped the cornstarch velvet. Slice thin against the grain, toss with soy + cornstarch, let sit 10-15 min before searing.

Broccoli is mushy / army green: Overcooked or too much moisture. Pat dry, high heat, single layer. You want charred edges in 3-4 min, not steamed in 10.

Rice is soggy / wet: Too much sauce on the rice, or too much broth when cooking. Stick to 1:2 ratio. Sauce should glaze the beef, not pool in the bowl.

Beef didn't sear / looks grey: Pan wasn't hot enough or too crowded. Wait for wisps of smoke before adding beef. Do 2-3 batches, not all at once.

Tastes like generic stir-fry: Add more sesame oil and finish with chili oil. The bone broth rice should carry the base flavor — if it's bland, you used water instead of broth.

Storage and reheating

Store: Store rice separate from beef. Broccoli can go with beef.

Reheat: Reheat with splash of broth to prevent drying. Avoid overcooking on reheat.

Lasts: 3-4 days in fridge

Estimated nutrition

~500 cal | ~45g protein.

The four-serving recipe's 500-calorie / 45g-protein adult estimate is separate from the filmed 2026 six-bowl batch below. That batch is about 455–490 calories and 41–42g protein per adult bowl before chili crisp; the topping adds an estimated 40 calories per teaspoon. The kid rice portion was not weighed, so no kid-plate total is claimed.

Filmed 2026: six adult bowls, separate kid plates

This is the batch shown in the video. Keep the original four-serving recipe above for its shared-sauce method; the filmed dinner uses the same bone-broth rice but puts all soy-sesame sauce in the adult beef-and-broccoli wok. The kids chose steamed broccoli, a smaller rice portion, and Polish sausage instead of the spicy beef.

The rice base is in the Bone Broth Rice recipe.

What the filmed batch used

  • •About 2 lb tri-tip, trimmed to roughly 30 oz (850 g) raw beef, sliced thin against the grain
  • •Bone Broth Rice: six adult servings plus smaller kid portions as needed
  • •About 3–4 cups broccoli for the adult wok, plus steamed broccoli for the kid plates
  • •3 tbsp soy sauce, 3/4 cup beef broth, and 1 1/2 tsp sesame oil
  • •4–5 garlic cloves, minced; 1 1/2 tsp grated ginger; about 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch
  • •1 tbsp cooking oil total for the adult wok
  • •For each kid plate: one Teton Waters Ranch grass-fed beef Polish sausage
  • •Optional adult finish: about 1 tsp chili crisp per bowl

How the filmed version came together

  1. 1Cook the bone-broth rice, allowing six adult servings and additional smaller kid portions. Steam the broccoli for the kid plates separately.
  2. 2Trim the tri-tip to roughly 30 oz usable raw beef. Slice thinly against the grain so it sears quickly and stays tender.
  3. 3Sear the beef in batches in the hot wok with the cooking oil. Avoid crowding; move the browned beef out while you build the sauce.
  4. 4Mix the soy sauce, beef broth, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch. Simmer in the adult wok, then return the beef and add the adult broccoli. Toss until coated and cooked through.
  5. 5Divide the beef and broccoli over six adult rice portions. Heat and slice the Polish sausage for the kid plates; serve it with their smaller rice portions and steamed broccoli. Do not put the adult sauce on the kid plates.
  6. 6Add chili crisp to the adult bowls only after portioning. The base-bowl nutrition estimate below excludes that topping.
Filmed-batch nutrition

Estimated per adult bowl before chili crisp: 455–490 calories and 41–42g protein. About 1 tsp chili crisp adds an estimated 40 calories, for roughly 495–530 calories topped. Beef grade, trimming, and ingredient labels affect the total. One Polish sausage is 180 calories and 10g protein; the filmed kid rice portion was not weighed, so no complete kid-plate macro is stated.
